520	King Saul has mercy on Agag. Having mercy on Agag is a Jewish trait, and it's our problem in every generation, that we have mercy
521	on the cruel.
522	We think our enemies are like us, that they're nice.
523	They probably want to gain something, that's how our minds work.
524	We don't understand that we're dealing with beasts.
525	Why?
526	Because we judge the enemy by ourselves.
527	But to be the king of Israel, you have to understand the nations.
528	You have to know who the enemy standing before you is.
529	Without mercy, without inhibition, to wipe out Amalek, from child to infant.
530	That's why the king of Israel must come with a bit of a mixture in him, a bit of goyishkeit.
531	A bit of their genes, so that he understands them, knows how to look at them, understands a bit how the gentile
532	thinks, how the enemy thinks, not only how he thinks himself.
533	Very bold things that the Shem MiShmuel says.
534	But it's broader than that, and it's already written in the Zohar and in many books.
535	The truth is that this is the whole arrival of David HaMelech in the world: three times, three
536	women take the initiative and do illegal acts, how shall we put it, non-
537	normative acts, in order to bring the next generation.
538	Who are the three women?
539	The first is the elder daughter of Lot, the second is Tamar, who sits at the crossroads,
540	lies in wait for Yehudah until he strays from the road, and then Peretz is born, Boaz's grandfather, as we discussed on the eve of
541	Shavuot, and the third is Rut herself.
542	As we said, why on earth would Boaz take her, a poor woman, barefoot, why on earth would...
543	a convert, why would he take her?
544	She waits for him at the threshing floor and lies at his feet, and he is in the middle of work, and his wife had just died the day before.
545	Women who do things almost by force, in order to advance, to bring into the world what Mashiach Tzidkeinu is.
546	Why is it this way?
547	It's written in the Zohar, in many books from all generations, the same idea.
548	In order to bring a great soul into the world, you must cover it with garbage.
549	You must cover it with excess, with refuse, so that the kelipot will allow this soul to arrive.
550	When you want to smuggle goods, how do you smuggle them?
551	Not wrapped in diamonds.
552	What do you smuggle them in?
553	In sand, in garbage, to confuse the guards at the border.
554	To bring into the world the soul of David HaMelech, this soul that will change things, that will bring the world to its rectification, it can't
555	work in a straight way.
556	You must blind the kelipot's eyes, you must confuse them.
557	So what does the Holy One, Blessed be He, do?
558	He stirs up such frightening events that the kelipot celebrate and say "Baruch HaShem," and they don't know that inside
559	the wheelbarrow He carried a diamond, inside the wheelbarrow He carried a pearl, He brought David HaMelech's soul into the world,
